That is mostly defined by the literal personality strengths and weaknesses of the person at the top. And that's been true of Mark and it's been true of Brett. Everywhere I go, that's who it is. You don't need a consulting firm to tell you, just go do a personality diagnosis on your founder. And the weaknesses thing is real. And your founder loves ambiguity and is perfectly happy with not making decisions. All that leads to is cultural dissonance. It leads to people being like, "Wait, what? I thought we said we care about moving fast and making aggressive decisions and it turns out..." So being really careful about what you say, because what people actually feel when it comes to culture is what you do and how you act every day.

You can never write anything down and you will still have a culture. It will be created through the actions and the decisions that you make and that your founder makes. So that would be a huge one.

(00:35:43):

If you were literally founding a new company from scratch with the same mission, how would you execute on that mission using a fully AI native approach?" And then, by the way, do you have useful building blocks that you can leverage from your existing product and your existing business, or are you literally worse off having this legacy asset versus starting something from scratch? And I don't think the answer is always yes or no. I think it just depends on the product.

answer.summary: Howie Liu cautions companies not to bolt a few AI features onto their existing product and declare the adaptation done; they should rethink how to pursue their mission with an AI-native approach.

sections.heading: The mistake to avoid
sections.content: Liu warns against adding “some AI stuff” to the marketing site and a couple of AI features, then calling it a day. Instead, he recommends a clean-slate question: if founding the company today with the same mission, how would it execute that mission in a fully AI-native way? Then assess whether existing product and business building blocks help—or whether legacy assets leave the company worse off than starting from scratch. He notes that the answer depends on the product.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately reflects Liu’s warning that companies should not add a few AI features or marketing changes and call that sufficient adaptation. It also includes his recommendation to rethink the mission through an AI-native approach, supported by S3. It makes no unsupported claim that information is missing.
